newsitem.title: CANADA: Production increases propel Talisman in '96. [CORRECTED 21:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Production increases propel Talisman in '96. [CORRECTED 21:41 GMT]

text.p: Sharply higher oil and gas production and prices pushed Talisman Energy Inc's results in 1996 to record levels, the company said on Thursday.

Talisman, which has launched a C$1.7 billion takeover bid for Wascana Energy Inc, rang up 1996 earnings of C$94.9 million or C$0.91 a share, more than double its earnings of C$40.5 million or C$0.42 a share in 1995.
Cash flow grew to C$697.4 million or C$6.71 a share from C$502.3 million or C$5.21 a share the year before.

"We did a lot of things very well in 1996 and it shows in these results," Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee said in a statement. "Talisman's cash flow per share has grown at an average rate of 40 percent per year over the past five years."
The company said its worldwide oil and gas production increased 16 percent in 1996 to 171,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day.
The total included a 29 percent jump in oil and gas liquids output to 99,960 barrels a day and a small drop in gas production to 647 million cubic feet a day.

The company said it realized an average oil and gas liquids price over the year of C$25.93 per barrel, a jump of 18 percent over 1995. Natural gas sales averaged C$1.94 per thousand cubic feet, up 20 percent.
Talisman, which had capital expenditures of C$1.1 billion in the year, said proved reserve additions totaled 186 million barrels of oil equivalent or 302 percent of 1996 production.
